gt-mit2025.title: MIT OpenCourseWare, 14.12 Economic Applications of Game Theory (Fall 2025), lecture notes and calendar
gt-mit2025.notes: Chapters on game representations, Nash equilibrium, backward induction, repeated games, Bayesian games, and auction applications. The lecture calendar also identifies minimax and auction sessions.

gt-yale.title: Ben Polak, Game Theory (ECON 159), Open Yale Courses, Fall 2007
gt-yale.notes: Mixed strategies, equilibrium, repeated games, asymmetric information, and auctions, with complete course lecture index.

gt-mitengineering.title: MIT OpenCourseWare, 6.254 Game Theory with Engineering Applications (Spring 2010), syllabus
gt-mitengineering.notes: Theoretical foundations including Nash and correlated equilibria, Bayesian games, mechanism design, revelation principle, and VCG mechanisms.

gt-computational.title: Tomas Kroupa, Computational Game Theory, Chapter 4: Two-player zero-sum games
gt-computational.notes: Explicit primal-dual linear-program formulation, weak and strong duality, and minimax theorem.

gt-mitmatrix.title: Gilbert Strang, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.065, Lecture 24: Linear Programming and Two-Person Games
gt-mitmatrix.notes: Connections among matrix games, linear programming, and duality.
